summary: Luther Forest tower erected 1924, state-run until 1970; taken down at Cornell Hill in 2010 and rebuilt at Camp Saratoga in Wilton; no source describes the original site today.

facts.design: 60-foot Aermotor fire tower with a 7 by 7 foot metal cab; model disputed (LS-40 per Starr and the Town of Wilton, LS-20 per NHLR)
facts.status_note: Taken down at Cornell Hill in August 2010 and re-erected at Camp Saratoga in Wilton; no source describes the original site today
facts.agency: New York Conservation Commission (erected the tower in 1924)

events.note: Erected by the NY Conservation Commission as a 60-foot Aermotor in Luther Forest; NHLR and Starr give the model differently
Noah LaCasse was the first forest fire observer, 1924 to 1935
State operation ended with the 1970 fire season; the tower was then decommissioned. The Saratogian names Jim Crammond as the last observer, without a date
William Mackay bought the tower from the state for $1, per the Saratogian; Starr says it went to Luther Forest for a nominal fee
Disassembled in August 2010; contractor David Vana cleaned and fixed the old steel, then re-erected the tower at Camp Saratoga
Dismantled at Cornell Hill in August 2010 and re-erected at Camp Saratoga in December 2010; NHLR dates the relocation to 2011
Dedication ceremony on May 14, 2011 at Camp Saratoga

corrections.why: Starr says the tower was dismantled at Cornell Hill in August 2010 and re-erected at Camp Saratoga in December 2010; the NHLR gives 2011 for the move, so the story notes both.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Starr and the Town of Wilton say LS-40; the NHLR says LS-20. The story reports both.
Starr says the tower was sold to Luther Forest for a nominal fee; the Saratogian says William Mackay bought it from the state for $1 in 1976. The story reports both.
Starr and the Saratogian put the dismantling in August 2010 and the re-erection in December 2010; the NHLR says the tower was relocated in 2011.

notes_for_editor: The Wilton record (us-ny-cornell-hill-at-wilton-camp-saratoga) covers the tower now at Camp Saratoga; this record covers the original Cornell Hill site. The Wilton record's second NHLR link is malformed (nhlr.org/nhlr.org/media/...). The Starr PDF is a two-column layout, so its quotes are short single lines. No source describes what, if anything, remains at the Cornell Hill site today; the 2011 guide rule could not be checked against a newer source.
